title: I made an open-source prompt kit for game spritesheets, with LLMs or ComfyUI
author: Alex_474747
selftext:
I made a small open-source prompt kit for generating game art assets.

It includes prompts for spritesheets, character action sheets, enemies, 2D environments, and concept art.... 

It should work with LLM/image tools and local workflows like ComfyUI or Stable Diffusion.

I’m using it myself for game-art prototyping and sprite generation, so I thought it might be useful to others too.

Repo: [https://github.com/lexlex47/game-art-prompt-kit](https://github.com/lexlex47/game-art-prompt-kit)

Would love any feedback on the categories or README

comments.author: angrylittledev

replies.author: angrylittledev
replies.body: People can tell, most AI pixel art is pretty obvious AI made, like these images here no one would confuse them with real pixel art.

replies.author: Alex_474747
replies.body:
I don’t think you looked at how it works closely enough. It’s not a one-click AI generator or a tool that creates the artwork from nothing.

You still need to draw the original image yourself. What it does is help restructure that existing artwork into a pixel-art style, while keeping the artist’s original intention and design direction intact.

comments.author: beelllllll
comments.body: How does it compare to using something like https://www.autosprite.io/ ?

replies.author: Alex_474747
replies.body: I tried it, but the results weren’t good enough for me to pay for it. That’s one reason I wanted to share this as an open prompt library. A lot of one-click tools are basically packaging similar workflows, so I hope this helps people understand and experiment with the process themselves.

comments.author: Southern_Charge5794
comments.body:
Why you don't add any GIF? I have played with animation generation in one sprite as 4k is tempting. But I reality those sprites looks as animation only on sprites and in GIF it looks like slop. I went into direction when you use image-to-video models like Kling O3. where you can start frame and end frame if you need loop animation. And results are stunning and smooth. In example there are 5 different animations where I extracted every third frame to keep sprite sheet size. You can generate pretty nice animation and convert it into sprite sheets. No offence, but for me it is a dead end and I found better solution.

https://i.redd.it/bqhrtl97v18h1.gif

replies.author: Alex_474747
replies.body:
Yeah, I agree yours may can give much smoother results, and there are already paid tools built around that. That’s probably why this post attracted many downvotes lol.

I see it as a different workflow rather than a replacement. Everyone can choose what fits their project best. I’m just sharing another option for people who know how to tweak prompts and want more control over the process.
